original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Children', 'Men')       and i_manager_id IN (9, 24, 27, 41, 59, 66, 78, 80, 83, 100)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('AL', 'MI', 'MS', 'OH', 'TX')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH store_state_counts AS (
    SELECT s_state, COUNT(*) AS store_cnt
    FROM store
    GROUP BY s_state
)
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count,
    SUM(ssc.store_cnt) AS cnt
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '30 days'
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'
JOIN customer c
  ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
 AND ca.ca_state IN ('AL', 'MI', 'MS', 'OH', 'TX')
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON c.c_current_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
JOIN item i
  ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
 AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Children', 'Men')
 AND i.i_manager_id IN (9, 24, 27, 41, 59, 66, 78, 80, 83, 100)
JOIN warehouse w
  ON ws.ws_warehouse_sk = w.w_warehouse_sk
JOIN store_state_counts ssc
  ON ssc.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
GROUP BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The join `store s ON s_state = w_state` (uncorrelated with store_sales) is a small cross join that multiplies every qualifying row by the number of stores in the warehouse's state. Replaced it with a pre-aggregated `store_state_counts` (one row per state) and changed `COUNT(*)` to `SUM(store_cnt)`, which is mathematically equivalent while removing row expansion entirely (score 9/10).
Converted implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI INNER JOINs, making the join graph unambiguous and allowing the optimizer to reorder freely (score 3/10).

Added the implied redundant predicate `d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'` — since d1.d_year=2001 and d2 is within 30 days after d1, d2 must fall in this range. This gives the planner an extra opportunity to filter d2 early (score 5/10).
Pushed selective dimension filters (d_year, i_category, i_manager_id, ca_state, ws_wholesale_cost) directly into JOIN ON clauses so they are applied during the join rather than after (score 4/10).
Added transitive equality `ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk` explicitly in the web_sales join to give the optimizer a direct fact-to-fact join edge on customer key (score 4/10).
